_comment: Worked example for GDX_SKILL_NEW_STUDY / GDX_SKILL_RECORD_NEW_STUDY. A short, fictitious 2-item scale, kept tiny on purpose to show every part of the shape (study, one instrument, one construct, one variable/indicator, one shared anchor set, two items feeding the same indicator, one of them reverse-scored). Real intakes will usually have many more items and possibly several variables per construct.

study.title: Pilot Study of Workplace Resilience in Remote Teams
study.objective: Explore whether a short resilience scale predicts self-reported burnout in fully remote employees.
study.method: Cross-sectional online self-report questionnaire, single wave.

instruments.name: Brief Workplace Resilience Scale
instruments.description: Authors: fictitious example instrument created for this worked example, not a real published scale.
instruments.instructions: Read each statement and choose the response that best describes how you have felt at work over the last two weeks.
instruments.phenomenon_description: Capacity to sustain effective functioning under work-related adversity.

constructs.name: Workplace Resilience
constructs.definition: Capacity to sustain effective functioning under work-related adversity.

variables.name: Recovery From Setbacks
variables.description: How quickly and completely the respondent bounces back after a work setback.
variables.operational_definition: Mean of items 1-2 of the Brief Workplace Resilience Scale.
variables.indicator_description: Mean Likert score of the two items feeding this dimension.

items.statement_text: When something goes wrong at work, I usually recover quickly.
A single bad day at work tends to throw off my whole week.
